SPEC.md (lines 1-357 of 357)
1: # JCROWN DIGITALS — Technical Specification
2: 
3: ## 1. Concept & Vision
4: 
5: JCROWN DIGITALS is a premium personal-brand website for Jediah Akeredolu — a digital publications platform that feels like stepping into a private library, not a storefront. The experience is confident, intelligent, and luxurious: deep blacks contrasted with restrained gold accents create a sense of exclusivity and trust. Every interaction is purposeful; every page tells Jediah's story first, then guides visitors to his work.
6: 
7: **Primary visitor journey:** Discover JCrown -> Learn about Jediah -> Click "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE" -> Browse and download available books.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 2. Design Language
12: 
13: ### Aesthetic Direction
14: Inspired by luxury editorial design and premium publishing houses — think Monocle magazine meets a private members' club. Clean, spacious, authoritative.
15: 
16: ### Color Palette
17: | Role | Color | Hex |
18: |------|-------|-----|
19: | Background (primary) | Rich Black | `#0A0A0A` |
20: | Background (secondary) | Charcoal | `#1A1A1A` |
21: | Background (panels) | Dark Gray | `#141414` |
22: | Accent (primary) | Royal Gold | `#C9A84C` |
23: | Accent (hover) | Bright Gold | `#D4B85A` |
24: | Text (primary) | Ivory | `#F5F0E8` |
25: | Text (secondary) | Muted Ivory | `#C8C0B0` |
26: | Text (dark bg) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
27: | Border/Divider | Subtle Gold | `#3A3A3A` |
28: | Success | Muted Green | `#4CAF50` |
29: | Error | Muted Red | `#E57373` |
30: 
31: ### Typography
32: - **Headings:** Playfair Display (serif) — elegant, editorial authority
33: - **Body:** Inter (sans-serif) — clean, readable, modern
34: - **Fallbacks:** Georgia, serif / system-ui, sans-serif
35: 
36: ### Spatial System
37: - Base unit: 8px
38: - Section padding: 80px–120px vertical
39: - Container max-width: 1200px
40: - Card gap: 32px
41: - Border radius: 4px (subtle, not rounded)
42: 
43: ### Motion Philosophy
44: - Scroll-triggered fade-up reveals: 600ms ease-out
45: - Button hover: 200ms color + subtle lift (translateY -2px)
46: - Page transitions: none (instant, for speed)
47: - Smooth scroll behavior with 80px offset for fixed header
48: - Focus states: gold outline, 2px offset
49: 
50: ### Visual Assets
51: - Icons: Lucide icons (line style, 1.5px stroke)
52: - Book covers: Admin-uploaded images, displayed in 3:4 ratio frames
53: - Portrait: Admin-uploaded, displayed in subtle gold-bordered circle
54: - Decorative: Subtle gradient overlays, fine gold dividers
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 3. Layout & Structure
59: 
60: ### Public Site Structure
61: ```
62: / (Homepage)
63:   ├── Navigation (fixed, transparent → solid on scroll)
64:   ├── Hero (100vh, centered, book mockup visual)
65:   ├── About Jediah (two-column: portrait + text)
66:   ├── What JCROWN Offers (three feature cards)
67:   ├── Download CTA (centered gold button)
68:   ├── Books Section (#books, card grid)
69:   ├── Newsletter (centered subscription)
70:   ├── Contact (two-column: info + form)
71:   └── Footer (minimal, links)
72: ```
73: 
74: ### Admin Structure
75: ```
76: /admin
77:   ├── Login
78:   └── Dashboard
79:       ├── Overview (stats)
80:       ├── Books Management (CRUD)
81:       ├── Homepage Content Editor
82:       ├── Subscriber Management
83:       └── Contact Messages
84: ```
85: 
86: ### Responsive Strategy
87: - Desktop: 1200px container, multi-column layouts
88: - Tablet (768px): 2-column grids, adjusted spacing
89: - Mobile (480px): single column, full-width cards, hamburger nav
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 4. Features & Interactions
94: 
95: ### Navigation
96: - Fixed header, 70px height, transitions from transparent to `#0A0A0A` on scroll
97: - Logo left, nav links right
98: - Mobile: hamburger menu, full-screen overlay
99: - Active section highlighting via scroll spy
100: - Smooth scroll to anchors with 80px offset
101: 
102: ### Hero Section
103: - Full viewport height
104: - Centered content: wordmark, welcome text, quote
105: - Subtle animated book stack or floating eBook covers
106: - Scroll indicator (chevron) at bottom
107: 
108: ### About Section
109: - Two columns: portrait (40%) + bio text (60%)
110: - Gold divider line between portrait and text
111: - Editable text via admin
112: 
113: ### What We Offer
114: - Three cards in a row (stacked on mobile)
115: - Each: icon, heading, short description
116: - Subtle hover: lift + gold border glow
117: 
118: ### Download CTA Button
119: - Large gold button, centered
120: - Label: "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE"
121: - Links to `#books` with smooth scroll + 80px offset
122: - Keyboard accessible, visible focus/hover states
123: 
124: ### Books Section (#books)
125: - Grid of book cards
126: - Each card: cover image, title, description, author, format badge, price label, action button
127: - Free books: "Download Free" button → direct file download (no login required)
128: - Paid books: "Get This Book" → checkout flow (Stripe or placeholder)
129: - Empty state: "New publications are coming soon" message
130: - Only published books shown
131: 
132: ### Newsletter Section
133: - Email input + "Subscribe for Updates" button
134: - Client + server validation (valid email format)
135: - Success: "Thank you for subscribing!" message
136: - Error: specific error message displayed
137: - Stores subscribers in database
138: 
139: ### Contact Section
140: - Fields: Name, Email, Subject, Message
141: - Client + server validation
142: - Success: "Message sent successfully" + form reset
143: - Error: "Failed to send. Please try again."
144: - Stores messages in database
145: 
146: ### Footer
147: - Brand name, copyright
148: - Quick links (scroll to sections)
149: - Privacy Policy, Terms pages
150: - Social links (configurable in admin)
151: 
152: ---
153: 
154: ## 5. Component Inventory
155: 
156: ### Button (Primary)
157: - Default: Gold `#C9A84C` bg, black text, 4px radius
158: - Hover: Lighter gold `#D4B85A`, translateY(-2px), subtle shadow
159: - Active: Darker gold, translateY(0)
160: - Disabled: 50% opacity, no pointer
161: - Focus: 2px gold outline, 2px offset
162: 
163: ### Button (Secondary/Ghost)
164: - Default: Transparent bg, gold border, gold text
165: - Hover: Gold bg at 10% opacity
166: - Focus: Gold outline
167: 
168: ### Book Card
169: - Dark panel `#141414`, subtle border
170: - Cover image (3:4), title, description (2-line clamp), format badge, price
171: - Hover: border brightens to gold, subtle lift
172: - Action button at bottom
173: 
174: ### Input Field
175: - Dark bg `#1A1A1A`, subtle border
176: - Focus: gold border, no outline
177: - Error: red border + error message below
178: - Placeholder: muted ivory
179: 
180: ### Navigation Link
181: - Default: ivory text
182: - Hover: gold text, no underline
183: - Active: gold text, subtle underline
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 6. Technical Approach
188: 
189: ### Stack
190: - **Runtime:** Node.js 18+
191: - **Framework:** Express.js
192: - **Template Engine:** EJS
193: - **Database:** SQLite (better-sqlite3 for sync operations)
194: - **File Storage:** Local filesystem (`/public/uploads/`)
195: - **Authentication:** Express sessions + bcrypt
196: - **Payments:** Stripe (optional, configured via env)
197: 
198: ### API Design
199: 
200: #### Public
201: | Method | Route | Description |
202: |--------|-------|-------------|
203: | GET | `/` | Homepage |
204: | GET | `/admin` | Admin login page |
205: | POST | `/admin/login` | Authenticate admin |
206: | POST | `/admin/logout` | End session |
207: | POST | `/api/subscribe` | Newsletter signup |
208: | POST | `/api/contact` | Submit contact form |
209: | GET | `/api/books` | List published books |
210: | GET | `/download/:bookId` | Download free book file |
211: 
212: #### Admin (protected)
213: | Method | Route | Description |
214: |--------|-------|-------------|
215: | GET | `/admin/dashboard` | Dashboard overview |
216: | GET | `/admin/books` | Book management list |
217: | POST | `/admin/books` | Create book |
218: | PUT | `/admin/books/:id` | Update book |
219: | DELETE | `/admin/books/:id` | Delete book |
220: | PUT | `/admin/content` | Update homepage content |
221: | GET | `/admin/subscribers` | View subscribers |
222: | DELETE | `/admin/subscribers/:id` | Unsubscribe |
223: | GET | `/admin/messages` | View contact messages |
224: | PUT | `/admin/settings` | Update site settings |
225: 
226: ### Data Model
227: 
228: #### books
229: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
230: - title (TEXT)
231: - description (TEXT)
232: - author (TEXT, default "Jediah Akeredolu")
233: - cover_image (TEXT, filepath)
234: - file_path (TEXT, filepath)
235: - file_format (TEXT, e.g. "PDF")
236: - price (REAL, 0 for free)
237: - is_free (INTEGER, 0/1)
238: - is_published (INTEGER, 0/1)
239: - download_count (INTEGER, default 0)
240: - created_at (DATETIME)
241: - updated_at (DATETIME)
242: 
243: #### subscribers
244: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
245: - email (TEXT UNIQUE)
246: - is_active (INTEGER, default 1)
247: - subscribed_at (DATETIME)
248: - unsubscribed_at (DATETIME)
249: 
250: #### contacts
251: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
252: - name (TEXT)
253: - email (TEXT)
254: - subject (TEXT)
255: - message (TEXT)
256: - is_read (INTEGER, default 0)
257: - created_at (DATETIME)
258: 
259: #### admin_users
260: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
261: - username (TEXT UNIQUE)
262: - password_hash (TEXT)
263: - created_at (DATETIME)
264: 
265: #### site_content
266: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
267: - section (TEXT, e.g. "hero", "about", "offers")
268: - content (TEXT, JSON)
269: - updated_at (DATETIME)
270: 
271: ### Authentication
272: - Session-based with `express-session`
273: - Bcrypt password hashing (cost factor 12)
274: - Session stored in SQLite
275: - Protected routes check session admin flag
276: - CSRF protection on forms
277: 
278: ### File Handling
279: - Multer for upload middleware
280: - Allowed extensions: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp (covers); .pdf, .epub, .mobi (books)
281: - Max file size: 10MB covers, 50MB books
282: - Files stored in `/public/uploads/covers/` and `/public/uploads/books/`
283: - Filenames sanitized with UUID
284: 
285: ### Security
286: - Input sanitization on all user inputs
287: - Parameterized queries (no raw SQL interpolation)
288: - XSS prevention via EJS escaping
289: - CSRF tokens on all forms
290: - Rate limiting on contact/subscribe endpoints
291: - Secure password requirements for admin
292: 
293: ---
294: 
295: ## 7. Pages & States
296: 
297: ### Homepage
298: - All 9 sections visible
299: - Books section shows published books or empty state
300: - Navigation highlights current section
301: 
302: ### Book Detail (inline in grid)
303: - Card shows all info
304: - Click download: triggers file download for free books
305: - Click purchase: opens checkout or payment modal
306: 
307: ### Admin Login
308: - Username + password fields
309: - Error states for invalid credentials
310: - Redirect to dashboard on success
311: 
312: ### Admin Dashboard
313: - Stats cards: total books, subscribers, messages, downloads
314: - Quick actions: Add Book, Edit Content, View Messages
315: 
316: ### Book Management
317: - Table of all books (published + draft)
318: - Add/Edit modal or page
319: - Upload cover + file
320: - Toggle free/paid, published status
321: 
322: ### Empty States
323: - No books: "New publications are coming soon"
324: - No subscribers: "No subscribers yet"
325: - No messages: "No messages yet"
326: 
327: ---
328: 
329: ## 8. SEO & Metadata
330: 
331: - Title: "JCROWN DIGITALS — Jediah Akeredolu"
332: - Description: "Discover digital publications and resources by Jediah Akeredolu. Explore books, access free resources, and stay updated with JCROWN DIGITALS."
333: - OG tags for social sharing
334: - Semantic HTML (header, main, section, article, footer)
335: - Canonical URL
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: ## 9. Setup & Deployment
340: 
341: ### Requirements
342: - Node.js 18+
343: - npm
344: 
345: ### Installation
346: ```bash
347: npm install
348: npm run setup    # Creates admin user, DB tables
349: npm start        # Runs on http://localhost:3000
350: ```
351: 
352: ### Environment Variables
353: - `SESSION_SECRET` — session encryption key
354: - `ADMIN_USERNAME` — default admin username
355: - `ADMIN_PASSWORD` — default admin password
356: - `STRIPE_KEY` — Stripe API key (optional)

{"path": "supabase/schema.sql", "content": "-- ============================================================
-- JCROWN DIGITALS — Supabase Schema
-- Run this in: Supabase Dashboard -> SQL Editor
-- Grounded in SPEC.md section 6 (Data Model + Security)
-- ============================================================

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- books: publications managed from the admin portal
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
create table if not exists public.books (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  description text,
  author text not null default 'Jediah Akeredolu',
  cover_image text,
  file_path text,
  file_format text not null default 'PDF',
  price real not null default 0,
  is_free boolean not null default false,
  is_published boolean not null default false,
  download_count integer not null default 0,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- Keep updated_at fresh on every update
create or replace function public.set_updated_at()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
  new.updated_at = now();
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists books_set_updated_at on public.books;
create trigger books_set_updated_at
  before update on public.books
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- subscribers: newsletter signups
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
create table if not exists public.subscribers (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  email text unique not null,
  is_active boolean not null default true,
  subscribed_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unsubscribed_at timestamptz
);

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- contacts: contact-form messages
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
create table if not exists public.contacts (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  email text not null,
  subject text,
  message text not null,
  is_read boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- site_content: editable homepage copy (about bio, hero, etc.)
-- key: 'about' | 'hero' | 'offers' | 'footer'
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
create table if not exists public.site_content (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  skey text unique not null,
  content jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

drop trigger if exists site_content_set_updated_at on public.site_content;
create trigger site_content_set_updated_at
  before update on public.site_content
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Row Level Security
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
alter table public.books enable row level security;
alter table public.subscribers enable row level security;
alter table public.contacts enable row level security;
alter table public.site_content enable row level security;

-- books: anon can only read published books
drop policy if exists "books_select_published" on public.books;
create policy "books_select_published"
  on public.books for select
  to anon
  using (is_published = true);

-- subscribers: anon may subscribe; only service role reads
drop policy if exists "subscribers_insert" on public.subscribers;
create policy "subscribers_insert"
  on public.subscribers for insert
  to anon
  with check (true);

drop policy if exists "subscribers_select_service" on public.subscribers;
create policy "subscribers_select_service"
  on public.subscribers for select
  to service_role
  using (true);

-- contacts: anon may send; only service role reads
drop policy if exists "contacts_insert" on public.contacts;
create policy "contacts_insert"
  on public.contacts for insert
  to anon
  with check (true);

drop policy if exists "contacts_select_service" on public.contacts;
create policy "contacts_select_service"
  on public.contacts for select
  to service_role
  using (true);

-- site_content: anon may read; only service role writes
drop policy if exists "site_content_select_public" on public.site_content;
create policy "site_content_select_public"
  on public.site_content for select
  to anon, authenticated
  using (true);

drop policy if exists "site_content_write_service" on public.site_content;
create policy "site_content_write_service"
  on public.site_content for insert, update, delete
  to service_role
  using (true)
  with check (true);

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Seed editable content rows (SQL Editor will upsert these)
-- Update the JSON here to change the site's copy.
-- ------------------------------------------------------------

  ('about', '{"title":"Meet Jediah Akeredolu","bio0":"Jediah Akeredolu is the person behind JCROWN DIGITALS, a digital platform created to share ideas, publications, and valuable resources with readers.","bio1":"Through his work, he aims to make knowledge easier to access and give people an opportunity to discover useful perspectives through digital content.","bio2":"Whether you are visiting to discover a book, explore a free resource, or learn more about his work, JCROWN DIGITALS is designed to make that experience simple, welcoming, and accessible."}')
on conflict (skey) do nothing;

**Supporting layer:**
- `src/lib/books.js` — fetchBooks, subscribeEmail, submitContact
- `src/lib/admin.js` — auth, site_content get/save, books CRUD, subscribers, messages
- `supabase/schema.sql` — `books`, `subscribers`, `contacts`, `site_content` + RLS + updated_at trigger + seeded About row

1: # JCROWN DIGITALS — Technical Specification
2: 
3: ## 1. Concept & Vision
4: 
5: JCROWN DIGITALS is a premium personal-brand website for Jediah Akeredolu — a digital publications platform that feels like stepping into a private library, not a storefront. The experience is confident, intelligent, and luxurious: deep blacks contrasted with restrained gold accents create a sense of exclusivity and trust. Every interaction is purposeful; every page tells Jediah's story first, then guides visitors to his work.
6: 
7: **Primary visitor journey:** Discover JCrown -> Learn about Jediah -> Click "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE" -> Browse and download available books.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 2. Design Language
12: 
13: ### Aesthetic Direction
14: Inspired by luxury editorial design and premium publishing houses — think Monocle magazine meets a private members' club. Clean, spacious, authoritative.
15: 
16: ### Color Palette
17: | Role | Color | Hex |
18: |------|-------|-----|
19: | Background (primary) | Rich Black | `#0A0A0A` |
20: | Background (secondary) | Charcoal | `#1A1A1A` |
21: | Background (panels) | Dark Gray | `#141414` |
22: | Accent (primary) | Royal Gold | `#C9A84C` |
23: | Accent (hover) | Bright Gold | `#D4B85A` |
24: | Text (primary) | Ivory | `#F5F0E8` |
25: | Text (secondary) | Muted Ivory | `#C8C0B0` |
26: | Text (dark bg) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
27: | Border/Divider | Subtle Gold | `#3A3A3A` |
28: | Success | Muted Green | `#4CAF50` |
29: | Error | Muted Red | `#E57373` |
30: 
31: ### Typography
32: - **Headings:** Playfair Display (serif) — elegant, editorial authority
33: - **Body:** Inter (sans-serif) — clean, readable, modern
34: - **Fallbacks:** Georgia, serif / system-ui, sans-serif
35: 
36: ### Spatial System
37: - Base unit: 8px
38: - Section padding: 80px–120px vertical
39: - Container max-width: 1200px
40: - Card gap: 32px
41: - Border radius: 4px (subtle, not rounded)
42: 
43: ### Motion Philosophy
44: - Scroll-triggered fade-up reveals: 600ms ease-out
45: - Button hover: 200ms color + subtle lift (translateY -2px)
46: - Page transitions: none (instant, for speed)
47: - Smooth scroll behavior with 80px offset for fixed header
48: - Focus states: gold outline, 2px offset
49: 
50: ### Visual Assets
51: - Icons: Lucide icons (line style, 1.5px stroke)
52: - Book covers: Admin-uploaded images, displayed in 3:4 ratio frames
53: - Portrait: Admin-uploaded, displayed in subtle gold-bordered circle
54: - Decorative: Subtle gradient overlays, fine gold dividers
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 3. Layout & Structure
59: 
60: ### Public Site Structure
61: ```
62: / (Homepage)
63:   ├── Navigation (fixed, transparent → solid on scroll)
64:   ├── Hero (100vh, centered, book mockup visual)
65:   ├── About Jediah (two-column: portrait + text)
66:   ├── What JCROWN Offers (three feature cards)
67:   ├── Download CTA (centered gold button)
68:   ├── Books Section (#books, card grid)
69:   ├── Newsletter (centered subscription)
70:   ├── Contact (two-column: info + form)
71:   └── Footer (minimal, links)
72: ```
73: 
74: ### Admin Structure
75: ```
76: /admin
77:   ├── Login
78:   └── Dashboard
79:       ├── Overview (stats)
80:       ├── Books Management (CRUD)
81:       ├── Homepage Content Editor
82:       ├── Subscriber Management
83:       └── Contact Messages
84: ```
85: 
86: ### Responsive Strategy
87: - Desktop: 1200px container, multi-column layouts
88: - Tablet (768px): 2-column grids, adjusted spacing
89: - Mobile (480px): single column, full-width cards, hamburger nav
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 4. Features & Interactions
94: 
95: ### Navigation
96: - Fixed header, 70px height, transitions from transparent to `#0A0A0A` on scroll
97: - Logo left, nav links right
98: - Mobile: hamburger menu, full-screen overlay
99: - Active section highlighting via scroll spy
100: - Smooth scroll to anchors with 80px offset
101: 
102: ### Hero Section
103: - Full viewport height
104: - Centered content: wordmark, welcome text, quote
105: - Subtle animated book stack or floating eBook covers
106: - Scroll indicator (chevron) at bottom
107: 
108: ### About Section
109: - Two columns: portrait (40%) + bio text (60%)
110: - Gold divider line between portrait and text
111: - Editable text via admin
112: 
113: ### What We Offer
114: - Three cards in a row (stacked on mobile)
115: - Each: icon, heading, short description
116: - Subtle hover: lift + gold border glow
117: 
118: ### Download CTA Button
119: - Large gold button, centered
120: - Label: "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE"
121: - Links to `#books` with smooth scroll + 80px offset
122: - Keyboard accessible, visible focus/hover states
123: 
124: ### Books Section (#books)
125: - Grid of book cards
126: - Each card: cover image, title, description, author, format badge, price label, action button
127: - Free books: "Download Free" button → direct file download (no login required)
128: - Paid books: "Get This Book" → checkout flow (Stripe or placeholder)
129: - Empty state: "New publications are coming soon" message
130: - Only published books shown
131: 
132: ### Newsletter Section
133: - Email input + "Subscribe for Updates" button
134: - Client + server validation (valid email format)
135: - Success: "Thank you for subscribing!" message
136: - Error: specific error message displayed
137: - Stores subscribers in database
138: 
139: ### Contact Section
140: - Fields: Name, Email, Subject, Message
141: - Client + server validation
142: - Success: "Message sent successfully" + form reset
143: - Error: "Failed to send. Please try again."
144: - Stores messages in database
145: 
146: ### Footer
147: - Brand name, copyright
148: - Quick links (scroll to sections)
149: - Privacy Policy, Terms pages
150: - Social links (configurable in admin)
151: 
152: ---
153: 
154: ## 5. Component Inventory
155:

157: - Default: Gold `#C9A84C` bg, black text, 4px radius
158: - Hover: Lighter gold `#D4B85A`, translateY(-2px), subtle shadow

1: # JCROWN DIGITALS — Technical Specification
2: 
3: ## 1. Concept & Vision
4: 
5: JCROWN DIGITALS is a premium personal-brand website for Jediah Akeredolu — a digital publications platform that feels like stepping into a private library, not a storefront. The experience is confident, intelligent, and luxurious: deep blacks contrasted with restrained gold accents create a sense of exclusivity and trust. Every interaction is purposeful; every page tells Jediah's story first, then guides visitors to his work.
6: 
7: **Primary visitor journey:** Discover JCrown -> Learn about Jediah -> Click "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE" -> Browse and download available books.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 2. Design Language
12: 
13: ### Aesthetic Direction
14: Inspired by luxury editorial design and premium publishing houses — think Monocle magazine meets a private members' club. Clean, spacious, authoritative.
15: 
16: ### Color Palette
17: | Role | Color | Hex |
18: |------|-------|-----|
19: | Background (primary) | Rich Black | `#0A0A0A` |
20: | Background (secondary) | Charcoal | `#1A1A1A` |
21: | Background (panels) | Dark Gray | `#141414` |
22: | Accent (primary) | Royal Gold | `#C9A84C` |
23: | Accent (hover) | Bright Gold | `#D4B85A` |
24: | Text (primary) | Ivory | `#F5F0E8` |
25: | Text (secondary) | Muted Ivory | `#C8C0B0` |
26: | Text (dark bg) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
27: | Border/Divider | Subtle Gold | `#3A3A3A` |
28: | Success | Muted Green | `#4CAF50` |
29: | Error | Muted Red | `#E57373` |
30: 
31: ### Typography
32: - **Headings:** Playfair Display (serif) — elegant, editorial authority
33: - **Body:** Inter (sans-serif) — clean, readable, modern
34: - **Fallbacks:** Georgia, serif / system-ui, sans-serif
35: 
36: ### Spatial System
37: - Base unit: 8px
38: - Section padding: 80px–120px vertical
39: - Container max-width: 1200px
40: - Card gap: 32px
41: - Border radius: 4px (subtle, not rounded)
42: 
43: ### Motion Philosophy
44: - Scroll-triggered fade-up reveals: 600ms ease-out
45: - Button hover: 200ms color + subtle lift (translateY -2px)
46: - Page transitions: none (instant, for speed)
47: - Smooth scroll behavior with 80px offset for fixed header
48: - Focus states: gold outline, 2px offset
49: 
50: ### Visual Assets
51: - Icons: Lucide icons (line style, 1.5px stroke)
52: - Book covers: Admin-uploaded images, displayed in 3:4 ratio frames
53: - Portrait: Admin-uploaded, displayed in subtle gold-bordered circle
54: - Decorative: Subtle gradient overlays, fine gold dividers
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 3. Layout & Structure
59: 
60: ### Public Site Structure
61: ```
62: / (Homepage)
63:   ├── Navigation (fixed, transparent → solid on scroll)
64:   ├── Hero (100vh, centered, book mockup visual)
65:   ├── About Jediah (two-column: portrait + text)
66:   ├── What JCROWN Offers (three feature cards)
67:   ├── Download CTA (centered gold button)
68:   ├── Books Section (#books, card grid)
69:   ├── Newsletter (centered subscription)
70:   ├── Contact (two-column: info + form)
71:   └── Footer (minimal, links)
72: ```
73: 
74: ### Admin Structure
75: ```
76: /admin
77:   ├── Login
78:   └── Dashboard
79:       ├── Overview (stats)
80:       ├── Books Management (CRUD)
81:       ├── Homepage Content Editor
82:       ├── Subscriber Management
83:       └── Contact Messages
84: ```
85: 
86: ### Responsive Strategy
87: - Desktop: 1200px container, multi-column layouts
88: - Tablet (768px): 2-column grids, adjusted spacing
89: - Mobile (480px): single column, full-width cards, hamburger nav
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 4. Features & Interactions
94: 
95: ### Navigation
96: - Fixed header, 70px height, transitions from transparent to `#0A0A0A` on scroll
97: - Logo left, nav links right
98: - Mobile: hamburger menu, full-screen overlay
99: - Active section highlighting via scroll spy
100: - Smooth scroll to anchors with 80px offset
101: 
102: ### Hero Section
103: - Full viewport height
104: - Centered content: wordmark, welcome text, quote
105: - Subtle animated book stack or floating eBook covers
106: - Scroll indicator (chevron) at bottom
107: 
108: ### About Section
109: - Two columns: portrait (40%) + bio text (60%)
110: - Gold divider line between portrait and text
111: - Editable text via admin
112: 
113: ### What We Offer
114: - Three cards in a row (stacked on mobile)
115: - Each: icon, heading, short description
116: - Subtle hover: lift + gold border glow
117: 
118: ### Download CTA Button
119: - Large gold button, centered
120: - Label: "DOWNLOAD BOOKS HERE"
121: - Links to `#books` with smooth scroll + 80px offset
122: - Keyboard accessible, visible focus/hover states
123: 
124: ### Books Section (#books)
125: - Grid of book cards
126: - Each card: cover image, title, description, author, format badge, price label, action button
127: - Free books: "Download Free" button → direct file download (no login required)
128: - Paid books: "Get This Book" → checkout flow (Stripe or placeholder)
129: - Empty state: "New publications are coming soon" message
130: - Only published books shown
131: 
132: ### Newsletter Section
133: - Email input + "Subscribe for Updates" button
134: - Client + server validation (valid email format)
135: - Success: "Thank you for subscribing!" message
136: - Error: specific error message displayed
137: - Stores subscribers in database
138: 
139: ### Contact Section
140: - Fields: Name, Email, Subject, Message
141: - Client + server validation
142: - Success: "Message sent successfully" + form reset
143: - Error: "Failed to send. Please try again."
144: - Stores messages in database
145: 
146: ### Footer
147: - Brand name, copyright
148: - Quick links (scroll to sections)
149: - Privacy Policy, Terms pages
150: - Social links (configurable in admin)
151: 
152: ---
153: 
154: ## 5. Component Inventory
155: 
156: ### Button (Primary)
157: - Default: Gold `#C9A84C` bg, black text, 4px radius
158: - Hover: Lighter gold `#D4B85A`, translateY(-2px), subtle shadow

I need to update the RLS so the admin (using the anon key in the browser) can read/write everything. But of course this is insecure. Let me think about the right approach.

The reality: the admin portal is a client-side SPA. It uses the anon key. For it to actually "change everything," we need the anon role to be able to write to books, site_content, delete subscribers, mark messages read, etc.

Options:
1. Loosen RLS to allow anon full access on all tables. Simple, works, but insecure (anyone with the anon key — which is public in the JS bundle — could edit).
2. Use an Edge Function with service_role to do admin writes, authenticated via the admin password. This is the "correct" way but requires Supabase Edge Functions deployment and would need the user to deploy. More complex.
3. Keep anon read, but use the admin password as a secret gate plus RLS policies that check a custom claim. Not feasible via anon key.

Given the project scope (a personal brand site, admin password gate, no backend), the pragmatic choice consistent with the existing setup is option 1: allow all-role access so the admin portal actually works, and document the tradeoff clearly. The admin password is a client-side gate anyway — it's not real security. I should be honest about this.

Done. Added a **Users** block to the admin portal.

## What changed
A new **Users** tab in `#/admin` that lets the admin see everyone who has engaged with the site — in one place:
- Aggregates **newsletter subscribers** + **contact senders** into a single de-duplicated list
- Table columns: User (name), Email (click-to-mail), Source (newsletter / contact), First seen date
- Marks a user's **first touchpoint** with a "First contact" gold badge
- Sorted by most recent first
- Empty state when there are no users yet

## Fix along the way
The first build attempt failed: my new `Users` component name collided with the `Users` icon imported from `lucide-react`. I aliased the icon to `UsersIcon` (used in the nav, the Overview stats card, and the new tab) — build then passed.

## Caveats / honest notes
- **Data dependency**: Users only populate once real Supabase credentials are in `.env` and the schema is applied — the portal reads from the `subscribers` and `contacts` tables. Without a configured Supabase it shows the empty state.
- **Source order**: Since it built on the existing tables, there's no dedicated "users" table; the block is a live roll-up of the two existing tables. If you later want a fuller user record (password logins, profiles), that would need real Supabase Auth — I can add that if you want.

-- ===
-- JCROWN DIGITALS — Supabase Schema
-- Grounded in SPEC.md section 6 "Technical Approach" (Data Model + Security)

-- books: admin-created publications (SPEC: books data model)
create table if not exists public.books (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  description text,
  author text not null default 'Jediah Akeredolu',
  cover_image text,
  file_path text,
  file_format text not null default 'PDF',
  price real not null default 0,

  is_published boolean not null default false,
  download_count integer not null default 0,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),

);

create table if not exists public.subscribers (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  email text unique not null,
  is_active boolean not null default true,
  subscribed_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unsubscribed_at timestamptz
);

-- contacts: contact-form messages (SPEC: contacts data model)
create table if not exists public.contacts (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  email text not null,
  subject text,
  message text not null,
  is_read boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- ===
-- Row Level Security
-- books: anon can read published books only; no anon writes
-- ===
alter table public.books enable row level security;
alter table public.subscribers enable row level security;
alter table public.contacts enable row level security;

-- books: PUBLIC read (only published)
drop policy if exists "books_select_published" on public.books;
create policy "books_select_published"
  on public.books for select
  to anon
  using (is_published = true);

-- books: block anon writes (RLS default-deny covers this when
-- no insert/update policy exists for anon)

-- subscribers: anon may INSERT; only service_role reads
drop policy if exists "subscribers_insert" on public.subscribers;
create policy "subscribers_insert"
  on public.subscribers for insert
  to anon
  with check (true);

drop policy if exists "subscribers_select_service" on public.subscribers;
create policy "subscribers_select_service"
  on public.subscribers for select
  to service_role
  using (true);

-- contacts: anon may INSERT; only service_role reads
drop policy if exists "contacts_insert" on public.contacts;
create policy "contacts_insert"
  on public.contacts for insert
  to anon
  with check (true);

drop policy if exists "contacts_select_service" on public.contacts;
create policy "contacts_select_service"
  on public.contacts for select
  to service_role
  using (true);
```

### 4. RLS policy mapping to requirements
| Requirement | Implementation | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| books: anon SELECT (published) | `to anon ... using (is_published = true)` | `books_select_published` |
| books: no anon insert/update | No anon insert/update policy written; RLS default-deny when RLS enabled | (n/a) |
| subscribers: anon INSERT | `to anon ... with check (true)` | `subscribers_insert` |
| subscribers: SELECT only service_role | `to service_role ... using (true)` | `subscribers_select_service` |
| contacts: anon INSERT | `to anon ... with check (true)` | `contacts_insert` |
| contacts: SELECT only service_role | `to service_role ... using (true)` | `contacts_select_service` |

Note on `update`: the task only requires "no anon insert/update" for books and none for the others, so no update policies are written — RLS denies all non-granted operations for anon.

### 5. Additional considerations / potential issues
1. **`updated_at` auto-update**: The books table has `updated_at` but no trigger to keep it fresh. Suggest an optional trigger, or note that admin updates should set it explicitly. Not required by the task, so left as an open decision.
2. **`service_role` note for admin reads**: The admin portal (P1, stretch) will need the `service_role` key from Supabase Dashboard -> Settings -> API -> `service_role` secret. That key bypasses RLS. This is a deliberate design choice driven by RLS matching "SELECT by service_role". It works, but be aware the service_role key must be kept server-side/secret (not in `VITE_` env vars). The current front-end client `src/lib/supabase.js:3-4` uses only the anon key, so service_role reads will need separate wiring.
3. **`to anon` vs `to public`**: For a Supabase app where signups aren't used, `anon` is the correct role (authenticated users are a separate role). Good.
4. **`unique` on subscribers.email** matches SPEC "TEXT UNIQUE" (SPEC.md:245). Good.
5. **`file_path`/`cover_image`** as TEXT mirrors SPEC's filepath fields and can hold Supabase storage public URLs or bucket paths. Consistent with SPEC.md:233-234.
6. **`price` REAL default 0** matches the SPEC "price (REAL, 0 for free)" (SPEC.md:236).
7. **Column ordering** — I kept the SPEC field order (SPEC.md:228-257) exactly as listed, satisfying "ground the schema in the SPEC data model exactly".
